title: Mean of a biased discrete derivative
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $0<p<1$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and choose a coordinate $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Under the product distribution of independent signs for which the probability of $-1$ is $p$, the mean of the discrete derivative of $f$ in coordinate $i$ is $\displaystyle\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\},\ i\in S}\widehat f(S)(1-2p)^{|S|-1}$, where $\widehat f(S)$ is the uniform Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$i$ is a coordinate among the $n$ coordinates
